title: Passkeys are not a trap
dot:
digraph G{rankdir=TB;graph[pad="0.2", ranksep="0.45", nodesep="0.3", bgcolor="white", fontname="Helvetica"];node[shape=box, style="rounded,filled", fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=12, margin="0.2,0.15"];edge[color="#5a6a7a", arrowsize=0.7];start[fillcolor="#2b6cb0", color="#1a4d80", label=<Passkeys are not a trap
A response to the viral “Passkeys are a trap” post>];subgraph cluster_claim{label="The viral post’s argument";style="rounded,filled";color="#c53030";fillcolor="#fff5f5";claim[fillcolor="#fff5f5", color="#c53030", label=<What the viral post claims
“Passkeys support attestation”
→ a hidden dial sites will slowly turn up
→ approved software/OS only, no LineageOS, no sharing
→ “throw in uBlock Origin” + FIDO + UK scanning
→ “not designed to prioritize your interests”
But this does not match how WebAuthn works.>];}subgraph cluster_reality{label="What the rebuttal explains";style="rounded,filled";color="#38a169";fillcolor="#f0fff4";r1[fillcolor="#f0fff4", color="#38a169", label=<1. Your passkeys don’t attest
Synced passkeys (iCloud, Google, 1Password, Bitwarden…)
return none when asked for attestation.
Consumer sites won’t request it – they’d lock out everyone.
Guidance has said not to ask for years.>];r2[fillcolor="#f0fff4", color="#38a169", label=<2. Attestation isn’t what you think
It reveals only the authenticator make/model (AAGUID)
plus a vendor certificate chain.
No OS, browser, extensions, root/jailbreak, firmware.>];r3[fillcolor="#f0fff4", color="#38a169", label=<3. The YubiKey recommendation backfires
YubiKeys are the authenticators that do attestation;
they ship with Yubico attestation certificates.
If you fear attestation, that’s the wrong solution.>];r4[fillcolor="#f0fff4", color="#38a169", label=<4. TOTP is a step backwards
TOTP is better than a password alone, but is phishable.
Evilginx relays password + code in real time.
Passkeys are domain-bound and resist MITM;
your example.com key won’t work on examp1e.com.>];r1->r2->r3->r4[color="#38a169"];}subgraph cluster_conclusion{label="Advice";style="rounded,filled";color="#2b6cb0";fillcolor="#ebf8ff";conclusion[fillcolor="#ebf8ff", color="#2b6cb0", label=<What you should do
Keep using passkeys!
Use a password/passkey manager you trust.
If consumer attestation ever appears, push back loudly –
but don’t abandon phishing-resistant credentials now.>];}start->claim;claim->r1;r4->conclusion;sources[fillcolor="#f7fafc", color="#a0aec0", style="rounded,filled,dashed", label=<Author background
WhyNoPasskeys.com · open-source passkeys PHP library
passkeys on Report URI · security testing
“I use passkeys everywhere I can — they’re the best thing we have.”>];conclusion->sources[style=dashed, color="#a0aec0"];}
